contracts.breakingRule: Pane, transient/focus or context boundary changes require consumer migration.
Descriptor field semantics changes require provider disposition.
Endpoint/canonical mutation changes require migration and consumer disposition.
Identity, schema, history, recovery or commit changes require migration and consumer disposition.
Provider descriptor, session identity or input/effect changes require migration and consumer disposition.
Visibility or eligibility semantic changes require affected-surface disposition.
Classification vocabulary or required-slot changes require profile migration.
Command identity, owner, availability or effect changes require registry migration.
Global shortcut/F6/Escape/input-ownership semantics require affected-family migration.
Source-truth validation or announcement lifecycle changes require presentation-consumer review; canonical truth may never move here.
Host lifecycle/descriptor projection changes require provider compatibility proof; domain payload semantics remain provider-owned.
Open/close/inert/focus/provider lifecycle changes require provider migration proof.
Scale token/projection changes require chrome geometry proof and must not alter document/canvas zoom, density or responsive semantics.
Enter/Tab/Backspace/caret/composition/shorthand changes require Structured consumer migration and IME proof.
Insertion/action/confirmation descriptor changes require route convergence and mutation-delegation proof.
Direction precedence/provenance changes require explicit rtl/ltr/platform/fallback proof and must never infer semantic language.
Sanitization/code/bidi/portable-rich changes require security and clipboard-boundary proof.
Drop-target/autoscroll/drag semantics changes require pointer-keyboard parity and canonical mutation delegation proof.
Group/search/disclosure/applicability changes require Structured and non-Structured profile proof; preference storage may never move here.
No M6 claim until a second genuine runtime provider exists; RuntimeAdapter causal truth and raw input semantics remain provider-owned.
State vocabulary/truth-conflict rules may not infer cause/copy/retry/status or build a generic async engine.
Host only consumes explicit destructive-risk descriptors; risk meaning and mutation remain external.
Host orchestration/renderer/bridge changes require real-consumer, owner-graph, read/edit, command-bus and browser proof; canonical document truth may never move into the host.
Read-inspection/outline/quick-jump descriptor changes require canonical tree/identity coherence proof and must not acquire DOM focus/scroll or canonical mutation ownership.
This proves Structured content compatibility only; it must never imply StickyNoteWindowOwner, NoteBindingAdapter, pin/always-on-top or separate-window lifecycle ownership.
Geometry/lifecycle/z-order/pin/popout capability changes require pointer+keyboard+viewport+focus proof; close/hide may never become source deletion and OS always-on-top cannot be fabricated.
Binding identity/availability/provenance changes require domain-shape, fail-atomic and source-identity proof; window/presentation identity can never become canonical source identity.

Note content must consume the same accepted Structured engine; duplicate final adapter/document identity, second editor engines, persistence claims, binding takeover or window ownership are forbidden.
Composition may mirror/project canonical owner truth for UI compatibility only and may not reacquire note window, binding, Structured content/history or persistence ownership.

Exact reference/key/compatibility/value normalization changes require collision, forged-metadata, missing/incompatible and provider-nonmutation proof; domain canonical meaning may not move into the shared owner.

Pair/session/result changes require exact pinned identity, deterministic diff, fail-atomic session, two-real-provider and domain-noncollapse proof; must not infer Review/Mastery/Evidence/Audit semantics.
Host changes require keyboard/focus/RTL-LTR/filter/inspection browser proof and may not acquire canonical provider or decision authority.
